data.name: Narayanan
data.gender_notes: Narayanan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Narayanan is a Hindu name derived from the Sanskrit words 'nara' meaning 'man' and 'ayana' meaning 'abode'. It symbolizes the protector and sustainer of all living beings. The name Narayanan carries the meaning “Lord of Man” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Narayanan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Narayanan is one of the names of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe.
data.etymology: Narayanan belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Man.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Narayanan total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Narayanan is a compound name, made up of the words 'nara' meaning 'man' and 'ayana' meaning 'resting place'. In this compound, 'nara' is replaced by the name of the goddess Narayani. So, Narayanan means 'Son of the goddess Narayani'.

historical_references.reference: The name Narayanan is derived from the Sanskrit term Narayana, which means 'resting place of the divine'. This term is used to describe Vishnu, one of the principal deities in Hinduism. Narayana is described as the supreme God, who preserves and sustains the universe.

Another reference to the name Narayanan can be found in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. In the Mahabharata, a character named Vidura, who was a wise and just advisor to the Kuru kingdom, is referred to as Narayanan. This usage of the name signifies a divine and wise leader or guide.
